name: Fridge Cigarette
description: Cold Diet Coke, bold espresso and a silky vanilla cloud. Fizzy, creamy, unexpected.
ingredients: Ice, to fill the serving glass
For the vanilla cloud: 30 ml whipping cream
For the vanilla cloud: 10 ml milk
For the vanilla cloud: 10 ml vanilla syrup
steps: Pull one double-shot espresso; allow it to settle briefly while you prepare the glass.
Whisk or froth the 30 ml whipping cream, 10 ml milk and 10 ml vanilla syrup into a soft, pourable vanilla cloud.
Add ice to a tall serving glass.
Pour 100–120 ml chilled Diet Coke over the ice.
Slowly pour the double-shot espresso over the cola to preserve the layers and limit foaming.
Gently spoon or pour the vanilla cloud on top, and serve immediately.
notes: Pour slowly: cola can foam when espresso is added. The vanilla syrup already sweetens the cloud.

name: Classic Affogato
description: Cold vanilla ice cream melting into a freshly pulled double espresso, finished with cocoa.
ingredients: A light dusting of chocolate powder or unsweetened cocoa powder
steps: Scoop 120–130 ml vanilla ice cream into a chilled dessert bowl or small glass.
Pull one fresh double-shot espresso using your espresso machine.
Pour the hot espresso directly over the ice cream just before serving.
Finish with a light dusting of chocolate powder or cocoa. Enjoy immediately.
notes: Serve immediately for the contrast between hot espresso and cold ice cream.

name: Salted Caramel Affogato
description: Classic vanilla affogato with a generous caramel ribbon and a tiny pinch of salt.
steps: Scoop 120–130 ml vanilla ice cream into a chilled dessert bowl or glass.
Drizzle 20 g caramel sauce over the ice cream.
Pull one fresh double-shot espresso and pour it over the dessert.
Finish with a tiny pinch of salt to make it a salted caramel affogato. Serve immediately.
notes: Use only a small pinch of salt; caramel sauce is already sweet.

name: Jamun Coffee Tonic
description: Muddled jamun, lime and sparkling tonic meet a fresh double espresso.
ingredients: Ice, to fill a 300 ml glass
steps: Deseed 40–50 g ripe jamun and gently muddle it in the serving glass with 5 ml lime juice and a tiny pinch of salt.
Fill the glass with ice.
Slowly add 120–130 ml chilled tonic water.
Pull a fresh double-shot espresso and let it settle briefly.
Gently pour the espresso over the back of a spoon to create a layered finish; serve immediately.
notes: Adjust tonic slightly for your actual shot yield and the amount of ice in your glass.

name: Sunrise Americano
description: Fresh orange, soda and espresso in a bright, sparkling sunrise of a glass.
steps: Fill a serving glass with ice.
Pour in 80 ml chilled orange juice.
Add 60 ml chilled soda water slowly.
Pull a double-shot espresso and slowly pour it over the drink for a layered sunrise effect.
Garnish with a fresh orange slice and serve immediately.
notes: Use cold juice and soda for clearer layers; espresso should be poured slowly.

name: Dark Chocolate Peanut Butter Iced Latte
description: Chocolate milk, honey-kissed peanut butter espresso and a fluffy honey cloud.
ingredients: 2–3 g Hershey’s chocolate powder, to make chocolate milk
8–10 g honey, for the espresso mixture
For the honey cloud: 30 ml whipping cream
For the honey cloud: 10 ml milk
For the honey cloud: 10 ml honey
Chocolate or cocoa powder, for dusting
steps: Prepare chocolate milk by mixing 2–3 g Hershey’s chocolate powder smoothly into 120 ml chilled milk (make a paste with a small splash of the milk first if needed).
Pull one double-shot espresso. While warm, thoroughly stir in 1 tbsp dark chocolate peanut butter and 8–10 g honey until as smooth as possible.
Pour the chocolate milk into a tall glass, then add ice.
Slowly pour the peanut-butter-and-honey espresso over the ice.
Whisk or froth 30 ml whipping cream, 10 ml milk and 10 ml honey until thick yet pourable.
Spoon the honey cloud on top and finish with a light chocolate or cocoa dusting.
notes: Contains peanuts and dairy. Stir peanut butter thoroughly into hot espresso before pouring; cloud toppings are best made fresh.
